abort.already_configured: This mqttcore cluster is already set up.
abort.invalid_discovery_info: The mqttcore app's announcement did not say where it answers.
abort.reauth_successful: A new API token is in place.
abort.wrong_cluster: That node belongs to another cluster than the one this entry follows.

error.host_not_allowed: The node does not answer to this name (HTTP 421). Use its IP address, its own DNS name, or the cluster's name.
error.https_required: mqttcore refuses passwords and tokens over plain HTTP while its HTTPS works. Turn on HTTPS under Connection.
error.invalid_certificate: The node's certificate could not be verified. Use the name on its certificate, or turn off certificate verification under Connection.
error.invalid_network: Enter up to four IP addresses or ranges (such as 192.0.2.10 or 192.0.2.0/24), separated by commas, or leave it empty.
error.not_mqttcore: That address answers, but not as an mqttcore node.
error.setup_needed: This node is not set up yet: set its OTA password in its console first.
error.token_not_accepted: The new API token was made, but the node did not accept it. Try again in a minute.
error.token_refused: The node refused to make the API token: {error}
error.too_many_attempts: Too many wrong passwords from this address. Wait a few minutes and try again.

data_description.ota_password: Used once to make a read-only API token for Home Assistant, then forgotten. Home Assistant never stores it.
data_description.restrict_network: The token then works only from these addresses or ranges (up to four). The address Home Assistant used to reach the node is filled in; leave it empty to allow any.

credentials.description: {host} answers. Enter the cluster's OTA password to make an API token for Home Assistant: it reads the status and system areas, and nothing else.

hassio_confirm.description: Set up the mqttcore cluster the {addon} app belongs to?
hassio_confirm.title: mqttcore through the Home Assistant app

data_description.ota_password: Used once to make a read-only API token for Home Assistant, then forgotten. Home Assistant never stores it.
data_description.restrict_network: The token then works only from these addresses or ranges (up to four). The address Home Assistant used to reach the node is filled in; leave it empty to allow any.

reauth_confirm.description: The API token for {host} no longer works (revoked, or limited to another address). Enter the OTA password to make a new one.
reauth_confirm.title: Make a new API token

data_description.host: One node of the cluster: its DNS name (as on its certificate), the cluster's name, or an IP address. Home Assistant learns the other members from it.
data_description.port: The node's HTTPS port: 443 unless you moved it.

user.description: Connect to an mqttcore node's admin API.

data_description.ssl: mqttcore accepts API tokens over plain HTTP only from the node itself (loopback).
data_description.verify_ssl: Leave on for a certificate from Let's Encrypt. Turn off only for a self-signed certificate.

cluster_unreachable.message: No member of the cluster answered: {error}

node_unreachable.message: The node did not answer, directly or through the cluster: {error}

token_refused.message: The node refused the API token: {error}

token_rejected.message: The node no longer accepts the API token: it was revoked or has expired.
